svg.text: Research ethics in a Ghanaian setting: where consent really fails
A signed form is evidence of a conversation. It is not the conversation, and it is not consent.
The pressures that quietly remove choice
The researcher is the nurse who will treat her
tomorrow. Refusing feels risky.
The chief or husband agreed on her behalf.
The payment is large next to a day's earnings.
The form is in English; the conversation was not.
Each makes agreement easier and consent weaker.
What repairs each one
Someone independent of care takes consent,
and refusal is stated to change nothing.
Community entry gains permission to approach;
the individual still decides for herself.
Reimburse costs and time; do not induce.
Translate, then translate back and compare.
Assent, consent, and who may agree for a child
The parent or guardian gives consent. The child gives assent, in words she understands, and a child's
refusal is respected even when the parent has agreed. Adolescents and people whose capacity fluctuates
need the question asked again rather than answered once at the start.
Three duties that outlast the data collection
If you find something clinically important about a participant, you act on it. That is not part of the
study; it is your duty as a nurse, and it must be planned for in the protocol beforehand.
Store identifiers separately and securely. And take the findings back to the community that gave them,
in a form its members can use.
